newsitem.title: USA: Ford idles Taurus, Sable plants for one week.
newsitem.headline: Ford idles Taurus, Sable plants for one week.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said it has idled its Taurus and Sable mid-size car plants in Atlanta and Chicago this week because of insufficient orders from dealers, affecting 4,700 hourly workers.

Ford said sales of the mainstay Ford Taurus and Mercury Sable models have been hurt by aggressive pricing actions by Japanese automakers, which have benefited by the weakness of the yen against the dollar. Ford also said the currency situation has resulted in a sharp drop in Taurus export requirements, primarily for Japan.

"As a result, there is an insufficient backlog of buildable dealer orders for Taurus and Sable to make up for the export decline and maintain production without interruption," Ford said in a statement.
The one-week shut down will idle 2,200 hourly workers in Atlanta, and 2,500 in Chicago. Together the two plants produce about a combined 10,800 Taurus and Sable cars weekly.
At the end of February, Ford said its dealers had a 62-day supply of Tauruses and a 51-day supply of Sables.
